title: Build an animated 3D film entirely in code
summary: A developer built a 70-second Japanese temple film from about 31,000 lines of JavaScript with no models or textures; the repo is tagged as made with Claude Code.
agent_role: The repo is tagged with Claude Code, but it does not say which parts the agent wrote versus the developer.
outcome: The repo reports a 24.4-million-triangle scene rendered into a 70-second 1080p60 film, taking about 4 hours on a laptop.
what_they_did: The developer generated an entire temple scene in code: buildings, statues, trees, water and sky. A script renders it frame by frame in a hidden browser and joins frames into a video. Music is added afterward.
how_it_went: The repo shows a finished 70-second film in 10 shots. The full render took about 4 hours on a laptop with built-in graphics.
worth_knowing: The first build and shader compile can take several minutes, and the full film render runs for hours, with built-in rest pauses to protect the laptop.
prompt: Help me build a small 3D scene of [subject] entirely in code with three.js, without any downloaded models or image files. Start with a plan of the objects, lighting and a few camera shots. Build it step by step, render still frames so I can review them, and then write a script that renders the shots into a short video with ffmpeg.

curation.rationale: An impressive, fully reproducible code-only animated film; the repo is tagged Claude Code but does not explain what the agent did, so the agent's role is thin.
